pro_course_detail.description:
Do you feel shy when talking to native English speakers?
Are you tired of people asking you to repeat yourself?
Are you tired of the blank stares and puzzled looks from native English speakers?
Is it frustrating for you when you think you've said something in the correct way, but they turn to another person and ask: "What did he/she say?"

If you can relate to any these questions, then these lessons are for you.

Generally, it takes between 10 and 12 lessons to make a significant improvement to your pronunciation. The lessons are structured in a certain way in order to make sure that you get maximum benefit and results from the process. 

Typically, we would start with a pronunciation assessment. I will make notes of the main problem areas. The 'goals' will then be presented to you in a systematic way.

Following the assessment, we would start to tackle the individuals goals: only one goal per lesson, as the brain naturally cannot cope with any more. We would typically start with some 'quick wins', working on the easier sounds, the sounds which are going to make the biggest difference to your pronunciation. As you go through the lessons, new goals are worked on (goals might change, as I will constantly assess you), and previous goals are reinforced constantly.

Each lesson involves:
- a quick review of the previous lesson.
- an introduction of the goal sound we will work on in the lesson.
- some ear training for the goal sound.
- some practice of the goal sound in words, phrases, and sentences.
- plenty of conversation practice in order to incorporate the goal sound in your speech. 

You will get plenty of correction throughout each lesson, a lesson document afterwards for your review/practice, and homework to practice and reinforce new habits. I will also allow you to record the lesson, as this will be so useful for you to review/practice and see what you're doing.

NOTE: if you have ANY specific goal, please let me know, and I'll see what I can do for you.

pro_course_detail.title: Pronunciation Assessment (currently free when you book a trial lesson!)
pro_course_detail.description:
This is the very first lesson that I recommend students take with me. 

Before the lesson, I will send you some instructions so that you can record at least one minute but no more than two minutes of your spontaneous speech. You will be given a list of ideas as to what you can talk about. Once you have done the recording, you will then email it to me so that I can transcribe it onto a Google Doc ready for our lesson.   

During the lesson (30 mins), I will share the Google Doc and the sound with you, We will then listen to one minute of your speech together and discuss any obvious problems with your pronunciation, noting them down on the Google Doc (also noting down things you do well!). This will be a good opportunity for us both to become aware of what your main problems are. It will also be a good opportunity for me to find out what you already know about the English pronunciation system (important for defining our later lessons). Throughout the lesson, time permitting, I will also give you some tips relating to your problems.

After the lesson, I will finish up in my own time and write a summary. I will then send you the Google Doc. You will also be emailed a printer-friendly PDF version. We can then come up with a plan action together on how to fix your problems. 

NOTE: This is only a quick diagnostic. I will only listen out for errors in relation to the 10 or so of the most common problems for speakers of your first language and also any other obvious problems. This is because there will usually be far more 'problems' (a lot of them not such a priority), and it would be impossible and demoralising for students to work on everything single little thing. Besides, as we go through later lessons, we would both become aware of any other problems and change your syllabus accordingly.

ALSO NOTE: Ideally, we would use VooV or Zoom for this lesson, as they are the best platforms for this purpose, and you also have the added benefit of being able to record the lesson.
